questions.q: What is the standard mechanism for a parent component to pass data down to a child in LWC?
options: Dispatching a CustomEvent that the child listens for
Writing directly into the child's shadow DOM from the parent's JavaScript
Setting the child's `@api` properties through HTML attributes in the parent's template
Calling `this.template.dispatchEvent` from the parent
questions.explain: Parent-to-child communication flows through @api properties: the parent sets values on the child's public properties as HTML attributes in its own template, and the value flows down automatically.

questions.q: Why is parent-to-child property flow described as 'one-way'?
options: Because the parent sets the value and the child reads it; the child is not supposed to mutate its own @api property to change what the parent gave it
Because the child can only read the value once, at component creation, and never again
Because @api properties can only hold numbers, not objects
Because events always flow in the opposite direction from properties
questions.explain: The parent sets @api properties; the child reads them. If the child needs to change what's displayed, that's handled through the upward-communication pattern (events), not by the child reassigning its own @api property.

questions.q: How does a parent invoke a public (`@api`) method on a specific child component instance?
options: By writing `{childMethod}` directly in the parent's template, the same way a property is displayed
By dispatching a CustomEvent named after the method
Public methods on a child cannot be called by a parent under any circumstance
By getting a reference to the rendered child element (commonly via `this.template.querySelector`) and calling the method on that reference
questions.explain: Public methods are not invoked through the template's `{}` data-binding syntax -- the parent needs an actual reference to the rendered child instance, typically obtained with `this.template.querySelector`, and calls the method directly on that reference.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why doesn't LWC support events flowing from a parent down to a child?
options: Because dispatching events is technically impossible inside a parent component
Because child components are not allowed to have any JavaScript event listeners

Because a parent already has a simpler, more direct way to pass data or trigger behavior downward -- through @api properties and methods -- so routing it through an event would add unnecessary indirection
Because downward events were deprecated in a recent API version but used to be supported
questions.explain: Events are meant for a component telling the outside world something happened, naturally flowing upward. A parent doesn't need that mechanism for downward communication because it already has direct access to the child's public properties and methods.

questions.q: In the `childForm` example, what does `this.template.querySelector('lightning-input')` inside `focusFirstField()` locate?
options: An input element inside this component's own rendered shadow DOM
An input element anywhere on the entire page, regardless of which component rendered it
The parent component's own template
A static resource named 'lightning-input'
questions.explain: `this.template.querySelector` searches only within the current component's own shadow DOM boundary -- in this case, the child component looking for its own rendered lightning-input element.
